topic: How to learn anything in half the time — the science of retention, plus the AI layer that makes it executable

hooks.text: Most of what you're learning, you'll forget within forty-eight hours. That's not a failure—it's how memory works.
There's a retrieval pattern that halves learning time. Almost no one uses it correctly.
Learning isn't about more reps. It's about timing the forgetting curve.
I've watched hundreds of professionals waste years re-learning what they already knew. The fix takes ten minutes.
You spend hours learning something, feel confident, then can't recall it a week later. That's fixable.

selection_reason: Hook 1 combines counterintuitive framing with immediate credibility—it reframes failure as system design. The two-sentence structure creates natural breathing room and the '48 hours' specificity signals research depth without claiming it. Pure James: calm, precise, no wasted words.
